notes.title: DevUpdate #8: 64x64 KM Gameworld
notes.content:
Discord: [url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url] 
Steam Wishlist: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1459700/Peasant_Simulator/#game_area_purchase]Wishlist Peasant Simulator on Steam![/url]
Bluesky: [url=https://bsky.app/profile/projectreign.bsky.social]Follow on Bluesky![/url]

[h2]Build #205[/h2]
Much of the recent work has focused on developing the game's underlying framework, with Build #205 specifically emphasizing improvements to level generation creation systems, streaming, and authentication.

[h2]The size of the Sandbox[/h2]
I can now confidently confirm that the final game world will span at least 64×64 km!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/OmAlPR7.png[/img]
This screenshot shows a sky-level top-down view of a 32 km terrain bridge I've built to test the map's scale. What you're seeing represents just one quarter of the final game world, which will extend to at least 64×64 km. Achieving this scale required significant testing and fundamental changes to how world modifications are created. The solution boils down to:

[olist]
[*] Tracking the location of anything "Removed from the Base World" - In a way that matches on both the client and the server, and in a way that is internally consistent.
[*] As players move around the game world, generating a list of potential objects/location pairs(trees, rocks, etc.) to spawn around them.
[*] Ensuring this list is [b]ALWAYS [/b]generated identically on both client AND servers
[*] Checking each potential spawn against a "Removed" database
[*] Preventing spawns for any objects previously removed
[/olist]
This means when you destroy a tree or pick up a rock, that item stays gone. Even if you leave the area and return later, the system remembers what you've removed and prevents regeneration. The system also works perfectly with hand-placed, non-regenerating objects, giving me the best of both worlds.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/X0Ee4MU.png[/img]
This is an example of how the above, while being seemingly straight forward, can go wildly wrong.
This image shows a location on the client, and the server, as binary - and we can see that there stands a single 1 out of place. These two should match. This imperceptibly small difference in binary totally breaks this system - so I've had to take great care to ensure that the client, and the server, internally, each agree on what has and has not been removed from the game world.

[h2]Procedural Generation and Persistence![/h2]
Building on the above system, I've begun work on terrain-based procedural spawning—essentially a proto-biome system. This allows certain trees to spawn only in forests and similar environment-specific spawning rules. I'm leveraging Unreal's "PCG" framework to achieve this, and its looking very promising.

The ultimate goal is going to be to create workflows and tools that allow me to procedurally fill the world with content that is designed to be exactly where it is supposed to be, and not fully randomly generated.

While the world will leverage procedural generation, its layout, landmasses, etc, will not change or be random. They will be fixed in layout for all players. The exact position of trees, sticks, rocks, etc, will be procedural however. This lets me craft and direct a specific world with specific landmarks and borders, while not having to take 400 years to build it.

[h2]Unreal 5.5 upgrade[/h2]
I've successfully migrated from Unreal 5.4 to 5.5. The transition broke a few things initially, but everything's stable now and running smoothly.

[h2]Shovels![/h2]
I've added "Shovel" as a new item type that allows players to collect certain ground objects like rocks, and also to gather soil, gravel, and other earthen materials based on terrain type. This will be essential for construction projects requiring specific amounts of materials (e.g., "300 pounds of soil" or "150 pounds of gravel").

[h2]Hand Hold / Equipping rework ![/h2]
I've completely reworked the game's core UX. Now you can simply press E to pick up any item you're looking at, and once in your hands, you can attack with it. So you can strike enemies with a fish, an apple, or a log, and each is capable of having unique attack data.

These represent the sort of "generic hand held" items - but then there are other more specific items which function specifically as combat weaponry - swords, spears, axes, bows, etc.

Additionally, I've implemented "thrust" item types such as pitchforks and spears, which offer unique functionality. Spears can now "skewer" meat, allowing players to carry multiple pieces at once, while pitchforks can gather hay and plant fiber efficiently.

[h2]Hotbar improvements![/h2]
I've fixed several hotbar bugs, with numerous UX improvements to make gameplay clearer and provide better feedback about equipped items.

[h2]Character Hand Upgrades![/h2]
I've upgraded the player hands to fully animatable character hands. Currently using the Unreal mannequin hands, this implementation utilizes the standard Unreal rig, meaning I can easily swap to masculine or feminine hands later without breaking anything. This groundwork also supports future clothing layering and character customization.

[h2]Developer cheat codes![/h2]
I've added /pktele and /pkfly commands to help with development. These won't be in the final game, but they've been invaluable during prototyping, making it much easier for me to navigate and test this massive world.

[h2]Player Persistence[/h2]
Players' characters now remain in the world when they log out. Eventually, I'll implement behaviors like having them automatically return home and lock their doors, but for now, they simply stand in place. Most importantly, when that player rejoins, they can repossess their character and continue where they left off—a feature made possible by my new authentication system.

[h2]Authentication.[/h2]
While not the most exciting feature visually, the game is now capable of authenticating players.

The server needs a reliable way to identify returning players to grant them control over their characters, houses, kingdoms, etc. To accomplish this, I've implemented a simple username/password system where the client hashes these credentials and sends only the hash to the server during login.
This means your actual username and password never leave your machine. 

For example, "MyCoolUsername|MyCoolPassword" when hashed with MD5 becomes the unique ID "9726dfb4e28603488c044018d65fcde5". The server can then use this to confirm your identity and restore your in-game possessions. This is admittedly a primitive system that I'll evolve throughout development, but it's perfect for my current prototyping needs.

[h1]Thanks for Reading![/h1]
Sorry for the lack of images, but this update was taking a bit to write a blog about and I didn't want to keep letting that all pile up. Have a good one!

notes.title: DevUpdate #7: Cooking, Crafting, Fire, Kingdoms.
notes.content:
Discord: [url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url] 
Steam Wishlist: [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1459700/Peasant_Simulator/#game_area_purchase]Wishlist Peasant Simulator on Steam![/url]
Bluesky: [url=https://bsky.app/profile/projectreign.bsky.social]Follow on Bluesky![/url]

[h1]Build #157[/h1]
Big post, lots of changes.

[h2]Fire Propagation[/h2]
Fire is something I've wanted in the game, and I've started including it into the background sim. It behaves about as you would expect, the fire searches for nearby entities, checks if they are flamable, and if so, lights them on fire - repeating recursively.  

[previewyoutube=ikN500Sf_xE;full][/previewyoutube]

Interestingly this has helped highlight some other performance issues I was having, and have since cleaned up! As a result, crops now are 13x more efficient then they were before! Which is great, because the game world needs to support hundreds of thousands of them.

Fire hasn't been added in a general case yet, its just something I'm testing in the editor - but as a proof of concept it does work. Fire represents unique challenges to the games design, and in a PvP sandbox every engagement could simply boil down to nuking all the forests in a region with fire. Which would be cool, but it needs to be balanced.

[h2]Kingdoms, and Territory[/h2]
[previewyoutube=_z7_SzAdpdo;full][/previewyoutube]
I've started working on one of the games major features - Kingdoms, Territories, and Holdings.
The basic idea is that each player can stake a claim to a specific area of land, and then physically update that border over time by securing new "Flags" into it. 

[img]https://i.imgur.com/aQpIRRc.png[/img]

As you can see in the video, territories won't simply be circles or squares, but actually organic borders that can be moved, and contested in War. If an unsecured flag is uprooted by a player or an NPC, then the territory will re-calculate based upon the flags left, allowing you to actually usurp other lands.

Eventually, the goal is to use territories to assert "ownership" over regions, and the resources they contain. Lords will also be able to specify what actions that Neutral and Allied players and NPCs within their territories are able to physically perform. If you want to allow "Peons" to farm, but not open the Armory, the system will eventually support this.

A wishlist feature for this could be storing the controlled territory over time in a "history" timeline, so anyone can explore the historical timeline of the area ... but that is for a future blog.

[h2]Physical Cooking[/h2]
Physical cooking is in the game now, and it works by actually placing items on, or in other heat sources:

[img]https://i.imgur.com/kQvSo7p.png[/img]
When placing meat next to a heat source, like in this image, the heat source will slowly impart heat to the item. If this item is "Heat Transformable" - it will change into a new item based on a series of rules. In the case of meat, it will become cooked!

[img]https://i.imgur.com/vbIN1Wj.png[/img]
Here I'm debug drawing the range of the fireplace. Because the blue rectangle is within the orange circle, the heat of the fire slowly imparts temperature onto the meat.

If the meat was placed closer to the red sphere, it would burn and convert into burned meat.

The funny thing about this is that after implementing it, I immediately felt like I was cooking on a grill as I kept adjusting meat to be close enough to the fire to cook quickly, but not too close to burn.

Cooking is handled by a list of Heat Transformable rules: 
[img]https://i.imgur.com/1Wtc0s8.png[/img]

In this case, Raw Meat can be come three things, 1. Cooked Meat, 2. Dried Meat, or 3. Charcoal. 

Which item it becomes depends on what temperature range it exists within, and for how long. As with all ECS things, this logic will scale to tends of thousands of items being cooked in the game world simultaneously. 

[h2]Proximity Crafting[/h2]
Following along from the cooking theme, I've also added "Proximity Crafting" to the game. Keeping with the theme of physically deforming items in the game world, to craft anything you place the constituent items on the floor in close proximity together, and then strike them with a hammer.

When a new player enters a world, they can pick up a rock - which functions as a primitive hammer. If they strike another rock with this hammer, this creates a chipped rock on the floor - their first primitive axe.

Eventually striking a pile of lumber and rope etc, will combine them into varying furniture. The system needs more work but functionally its there.

[h1]Thanks for Reading![/h1]
Thanks for reading! In the coming weeks I'll be improving the kingdom system, adding user interface to interact with it, naming, and server wide notifications for when a new kingdom is founded, or destroyed.

notes.title: DevUpdate #6: Rot, Construction, and Farming
notes.content:
Howdy again! Feel free to [url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url] if you wish to follow the development more closely, and if you want to help the game succeed, feel free to and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1459700/Peasant_Simulator/#game_area_purchase]Wishlist Peasant Simulator on Steam![/url]. Thank you.


[h1]Build #148[/h1]
Rather than including the change list at the bottom of every post, I think it would be more prudent to simply include the current build of the game at the top. This is currently the 148th Steam build.

[h1]Farming Benchmarking.[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/cngMUT7.png[/img]

I recently conducted a farming Benchmarking test with a three players total, and the systems seemed to scale very well! We created a plot of several thousand tilled soil patches, and the game / server didn't blink. So performance is looking good! It will be exciting to see large groups of players coordinating to farm large swathes of land.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/D5WqrW1.png[/img]

The cool part about this is that you need to move all of the sticks, rocks, and tree logs etc, off of the farmable soil to be able to till it. So it wasn't simply spamming soil plots, it was several players making meaningful changes to the game world, in a fashion similar to the final gameplay, and the benchmarking passed with flying colors.

[h1]Rotting and Perishability[/h1]
Items in the game world can now rot into other items!
Each perishable item in the game world maintains an internal tracker of how rotten they are, and when this value hits zero, they destroy themselves, and can optionally leave behind piles of effluent and other items.

For example, Plant Fibers, which you get from chopping down grass and other foliage, will now perish into 2 "Rot" items, after 30 seconds:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/CGkvwli.png[/img]

Rot is also a perishable item, but it rots into nothingness:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/fWW86u7.png[/img]

For the sake of testing, Deer corpses rot into "flesh" and "flesh" rots straight back into deer corpses, back and forth infinitely.

None of these numbers of behaviors are final of course, just testing values. In the real game rot and perishability will be a slow and gradual process that takes days to occur. It isn't supposed to be a surprise to the player.

Interestingly enough, I can respond to entities dying due to rot very easily - perhaps propagating some sort of "disease" value into the immediate surroundings. FLECS makes this sort of behavior really easy to accomplish technically

[h1]Building Construction and Deconstruction.[/h1]
I've done a lot of work to move buildings over to FLECS, and that's looking good now.
1. You create construction blueprints that require items and labor
2. The building then consumes items added to it which are required to build it.
3. Once the building has its required items, you then apply labor to it (this will be via the hammer in the future).
4. Once it gains enough labor, the building will become fully constructed, and live within the ECS world.

This will need to be stress tested at some point in the near future, but it should hold up as well as everything else does currently.

[h1]Item Movement Polish.[/h1]
1. I've had to refactor item movement a little bit, just to make it a bit easier to actually grab and locate items in the game world, instead of aiming exactly at them.
2. I've added a subtle auto aim to item picking up which makes it slightly easier to grab stuff now
3. The system traces into the world, and grabs the closest item to where you're aiming, so even if you're looking next to but not quite at a specific item, your hands will grab the item. I noticed that it was mentally quite taxing having to exactly aim at an item every single time I wanted to pick it up - this helps reduce that mental load.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/awp17gy.png[/img]
Here you can see two traces coming off the aim point, seeking the two nearest sticks.

4. This did however highlight a new problem - its actually sort of a nightmare to place items back into the world now. Mainly because this new method of grabbing them makes drop spamming really hard, and secondly because if you're holding 15 items, the player won't want to perform 15 actions to drop them all. So now you can simply right click once, and all of those items will be dropped into the world in one go, roughly around where you're aiming with some random scattering. If you're aiming at nothing or into the air, they will be dropped around your feet.

[img]https://i.imgur.com/A5VPKd5.png[/img]
And here is what it looks like. This is a collection of 5 sticks that I have dropped back into the game world.



[h1]Close item graph[/h1]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/dxDS49D.png[/img]

Items now keep track of what other items are "close" to them in the game world, shown by the orange line in the above screenshot.

I don't do anything with this information yet, but it will be instrumental in fire and disease propagation. The basic idea being that if something is on fire, it already knows what is next to it, and simply can increase its "temperature" value. That other entity can then combust into flame once its temperature is high enough, and repeat the process. This is an expression of "The Space Time" tradeoff - by storing these connections long before I need to use them, instead of calculating them when the object catches fire, I can make fire propagation very cheap when it eventually needs to occur.

[h1]Thanks for Reading![/h1]
Thanks for reading! As always if you want to support the  development of Peasant Simulator, feel free to [url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url], and [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1459700/Peasant_Simulator/#game_area_purchase]Wishlist Peasant Simulator on Steam![/url]

notes.title: DevUpdate #4: Fishing
notes.content:
[h1]Hello again![/h1]
[url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url] to follow updates as they happen and be part of the community.
[h2]Fishing[/h2]
Fishing is now making its way into the game as a fully interactive system.
[olist]
[*] Bodies of water now support fish populations, with fish visibly swimming across the surface. Additionally these surfaces will LOD down to no fish when the player leaves the area, when the player re-enters the area. Eventually the same fish will respawn, but for now its random.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/8ceb8b2e4ca83fbc7ff72757be995b6290bc9f35.png[/img]
[*] Players can cast a lure into the game world with a simple click.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/7502c28b1abcd06f36349ed15fc8ceb860bc6053.png[/img]
[*] When the lure lands, it generates a noise visualized by a white sphere.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/cde9380cab7122a75068a2539c63680b43945b8c.png[/img]
[*] Fish within range of the noise will be startled and quickly swim away. Retrieving the lure also creates noise, making careful timing important.
[*] Once in the water, the lure drifts along its cast trajectory and is gradually influenced by wind direction.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/8472f96762aabf6638a22b3fd350461555113bae.png[/img]
[*] The lure periodically checks for nearby fish — the eventual goal is for the lure to actively attract them.
[*] When a fish is nearby, players can release the mouse button to attempt a catch.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/878a96c39bd58d2298ee9bdb022b86992fb78985.png[/img]
[*] If the lure is close enough, the fish will be hooked and caught.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/896f625b60bcad90cae2ae9619fb5a23d28053a6.png[/img]
[*] If you're just outside the catch range, you'll miss — and the retrieval noise will scare the fish away.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/f769d4f71dfa33b1e866c883dff8400bee562cab.png[/img]
[/olist]
The system still needs work, but the aim is to create a fishing experience that is manual, rewards patience, prediction, and observation, with the ability for players to tactically coordinate by shepherding fish.
[h3]Future Fishing Features[/h3]
[list]
[*] Spear fishing — Equip a sharp weapon, wait, and strike for a dead fish.
[*] Hand fishing — Crouch in shadows, wait, and grab to catch live fish.
[*] Physically hauling caught fish, requiring players to carry them by hand.
[*] Ecosystem balance — Overfishing could deplete lakes entirely.
[*] Introducing fish stocking — Add certain species to lakes to control populations.
[*] Fish responding to player shadows and movement.
[*] Better fishing rods and lures improving catch rates.
[/list]
[h2] Community! [/h2]
Thank you for reading, as always the link to the discord is here: 
[url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url].

notes.title: DevUpdate #3: A world of lootable items.
notes.content:
[h1]Hello again![/h1]
[url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url] to follow updates as they happen and be part of the community.

[h2]Technical Update![/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/52073de82fc39bd7e74f0163613722508ac0b2da.png[/img]
[i]Over 50 000 networked, placeable, lootable, destroyable items spread out throughout the game world.
[/i]

In Peasant simulator, the world will be filled with interactive items. Not only that, but players will be able to place and customize their spaces, potentially creating thousands of props in their villages. This is a technical post that is going to explain how I pulled this off.

These changes will underpin all of the gathering, building, and networking systems throughout Peasant Simulator.

[b][i]This post is going to have a lot of jargon in it, so I apologize in advance.[/i][/b]

[h3]Gathering from the world[/h3]
How hard can cutting a down a tree or picking up an item be, really? You just look at the thing, left click, and either you loot the apple or the tree falls down ... Can't be that hard right? Wrong. Follow along if you wanna find out why.

[h3]Problem A - The Internet[/h3]
You will often hear people comment that making a multiplayer game is hard, and they arn't wrong.

In Peasant simulator, the game world will be littered with interactable items. Players will be able to level forests, pick wild foliage, and place items all throughout their environment in a myriad of ways. 

This means a lot of information needs to be sent (replicated) over the network to and from varying computers.

But if you try and replicate a lot of information at once, you hit a hard limit brick wall, and Unreal will crash the program. It does this for the sake of the rest of the gameplay not falling apart, so its a good thing, but if want to replicate a LOT of things to a player,  it represents a problem.

[h3]Divide and conquer[/h3]
If you and a friend host a new game and make a bunch of changes to the world, via editing, building, looting, etc, everything is fine. Even for many hours.

But eventually a new player will connect (referred to as a Late Join), and the server will try and tell them about the game world. It is at this point that this bit of assembly code will say hi:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/8a0d98f2b6baf2f8f9b38372fa53a6d0e6fa36f1.png[/img]

And if you're in the editor, you'll be greeted by this red text:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/7367bd1232ef26192b9c35dca51fa29cd4ec3a26.png[/img]
Congratulations. You just crashed the server.

We can't send it all at once - we have a hard limit of 65536 bytes per packet. If we cant send it all at once, we send it in chunks - Chunked Replication, and it looks something like this:


[h3] The Algorithm [/h3]
[olist]
[*] The player attempts to place an item into the world
[*] The game asks the ItemEdits system if any player has ever edited this area before.
[*] If no, the system creates an "Edit Chunk", and remembers it
[*] The system then stores the edit inside of the this "Edit Chunk", but only if the Edit Chunk doesn't already have too many edits inside of it (otherwise we would defeat the purpose of this whole approach). So, only store an edit if there are <512 existing edits in the chunk, and if not? We create a new chunk and insert them there.
[*] Later, the system determines which chunks a connected player needs to know about (whichever ones are close to the edit in the game world.)
[h3] Problem B - What does it mean to be "close"?[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/2141abda2671dfc1b16d90699be44cfb43ac020e.png[/img]
Determining which chunk is closest to a location, in a sea of chunks, is potentially very costly. We cant just check each one, so we need a way of cutting the data set down to a smaller subset of ones more relevant to the problem ... oh would you look at that its our old friend Divide and Conquer again.
[olist]
[*] Whenever a chunk is created, we snap (quantize) its location to a grid. Like a big checkerboard across the game world.
[*] We then insert the chunk AND this location into a "Spatial Acceleration Structure", known as a "Spatial Hashmap" (other structures exist and they all have their pros and cons, but Spatial Hashmaps are fast enough, and very easy to write.)
[*] Whenever we wish to determine if a chunk is close to a given location (like where you wish to drop an item for example), we take that location, Quantize it to the grid, and ask the Spatial Hashmap if there are any associated with that location. There may be many.
[*] We now iterate over these chunks, and check their changes, finding the one that matches the location we're trying to edit.
[/olist]
[*] Once we know which chunks that player needs, we serialize the chunks into binary, ensuring that we always stay below a total serialized amount of 65535 bytes. If we get close to going over 65535, we halt. We will handle the rest later.
[*] At this point, the system has correctly determined, in this frame, the maximum amount of edits it can hand to a client, for this specific location, without crashing the server! Yay!
[/olist]

[h3]Problem C - Rendering[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/2027f219a0a9d69dbc74abb2bc0d6f11dd17ba07.png[/img]
[i]Whoever invented geometry sucks.[/i]

When dealing with potentially thousands of interactive items in the world, rendering becomes a significant bottleneck on both CPU and GPU resources.

Luckily in Unreal 5, we have access to Nanite which will significantly mitigate a lot of the costs associated with drawing the triangles of the items to the screen. So I leverage that, which mitigates most of the problems (while creating some other problems of its own). But Nanite doesn't magically solve everything. 

The naive approach of creating an individual actor for every tree, rock, or placed item would be catastrophically expensive, even with Nanite, and this mistake gets made a lot. Unreal has many "Per Object costs" (non technical term I just made up) associated with rendering things actor by actor. It could probably do it at or slightly below 60 frames per second, but ideally I would like more.

I approach the problem the same way I do with Chunked Replication - but with Chunked Rendering. 

[h3]The other Algorithm[/h3]
[olist]
[*] When Item Edit Chunks replicate down to our machine, we send a "Root Position" for the chunk also.
[*] If no "Item Edit Renderer" is near that location, we create one. This will be a new actor, and we pay some costs here.
[*] We then iterate all of the individual Edits stored within the Item Edit Chunk, and create a new "Render Instance" for that edit, and begin drawing them to the screen using Unreals Instanced Static Mesh components. In the standard rendering path Instanced Static Meshes can be slower then Unreals specialized Hierarchically Instanced Static Mesh components, but because we're using Nanite it can shortcut the need for the HISM component, and render its specific ISM component which is much faster then both.
[*] Tadaa! We just received an "Item Edit" from the server
[/olist]

If you do this right, you can have A LOT of "things" in your multiplayer world:

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/e5b2e569a84443de55cf3671c9fb058df71e1952.png[/img]
[i]Over 50 000 networked items spread out throughout the game world.[/i]

These things, in the final game, will be things like mushrooms, sticks, piles of hay, firewood, animal droppings, corpses, flesh, dropped equipment, etc. I will generalize this too to include things like building elements, furniture, etc.

[h3]Divide and conquer continued[/h3]
You may have noticed that we solved all three problems in basically the exact same way. Divide the problem into some smaller set of problems, and see if solutions can attack these smaller portions directly.

Pretty much every video game ever made hinges on this concept. Rendering, Physics, Networking, everything. Its a rather elegant way that almost always tends to effectively break larger problems down into more manageable problems that the computer can crunch. Not always, but most of the time.

[h3]Final thoughts[/h3]
There are many different ways that many games will attack this problem. This solution works for mine , but who knows, one day it might change again. Whatever code the game needs is what it will get.

[h2] Community! [/h2]
A few people with access to the game were instrumental in helping me test and find the varying  crashes and bugs associated with building this system. Thank you for your time. As always the link to the discord is here: 
[url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url].

notes.title: DevUpdate #2: Farming!
notes.content:
[h1]Hello again![/h1]
[url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url] to see updates as they happen.

So since restarting the games development, I've actually managed to put a good chunk of work into it, and I've gotten a lot done, and I want to write some dev blogs about it, so over the coming weeks I'm going to be retroactively talking about the content I've added in periodic dev updates.

So in this post we're going to talk about [b]farming and items[/b]. 

[h2] Items [/h2]
Items are interesting in games because pretty much every game has them but no two implementations are the same. In Peasant Simulator, I've implemented what I'm calling "partial items" - meaning that instead of 1x Raw Meat, you have 1.25lb's of Raw Meat. If a recipe calls for 0.2lbs of Raw Meat to create some Jerky for instance, you would be able to create many bits of jerky from a single item of 1.25lbs of Raw Meat. 

Farming items are treated the exact same way. When you fill your bucket up with water, the bucket contains an Item called "Brackish Water", and has a capacity to hold say 2lbs of water. 

Your seed bag can hold up to 10lbs of any ONE type of seed. So you can't fill it with all sorts, you need to be specific.

I think this could be a neat idea to handle the games many item needs, so I'm going to roll with it for a while and see if it is fun, boring and tedious.

[h2] Farming [/h2]
I've written a lot of the backend features to support farming in the game, and the steps to engage in the mechanic at the moment roughly are as follows:

[olist]
[*] Equip your Hoe - Right now all players start with all tools, and cannot remove them, so for now all players will have access to a hoe.
[*] Find a patch of farmable soil - The map has varying splotches of different color, and they represent either farmable area, or non farmable area.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/f3ea18359a72978606b6874c4fdce9dafd2f83ef.png[/img]
[*] 2. Till it with your hoe - This spawns a "plot" actor into the world, that can be interacted with to conduct farming. You can remove them by striking them with your hoe.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/e36e1c28b0ddcaa66bc9dcbcdc3dcde18e10b6cd.png[/img]
[*] Equip your speedbag, and fill it with seeds found in the wild. - The idea here is that you will need to fill a "bag" item with seeds, and then empty that bag into your field. So you might fill it with 20 pounds of barley seed, then plant that seed into say 50 plots.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/39e778167fd6e440336948271791569db8d3d667.png[/img]
[*] Pour the seeds onto the tilled soil - This embeds the seed type into the  tilled soil, and it begins to grow, if watered. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/8f0bbfade13c0b29233c0fc3276594d26ea237a6.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/7740d50a140bb267d40581c28fb726aff7fa93db.png[/img]
[*] Find a source of water - The map has many sources of water. They have a natural capacity, and a natural replenishment rate. If you drain them fully, it will take some time for the water to return to that water source. 
[*] 6. Use your bucket to draw water from the source.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/4bbb44450cd6ec102b644d6c521ade48f5353f19.png[/img]
[*] 7. Haul this bucket of water to the soil to water it. - The idea here being that players will need to make risk reward decisions based upon how close they can find tillable soil patches to water sources, as they wish to mitigate the travel time hauling water. Eventually they will be able to irrigate and build wells, etc. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/153f705cb32eef33a47c5cda22801e49c37c5f68.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/5500f8d20a35a6347dce33207c2eedd79caea7bf.png[/img]
[*] Wait for the crops to crow - A crop will receive growth progress provided its watered. Currently there  are no seasonal factors, crops simply grow. Its very basic
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/9c3b7ffb7b96f9dd3870ea89cded8fe1445298e5.png[/img]
[*] When fully grown, cut them down with a scythe - Equip your scythe, and attack the crops! They will destroy themselves and their seed plot, and dump their fully grown crop onto the floor. I haven't thought about how to interact with tubers etc yet.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/e348891ed0140c52712c14d0c0c6ef0e7522f5dc.png[/img]
[*] Haul the crops into storage bins either by hand or pitchfork. - By default you can pick some wheat up with your hands, but you cant haul much of it, its sort of like water in a bucket. 
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/77bcdd6463d987fa344a6d03da71f2fedc4604db.png[/img]
But with a pitch fork, you can carry up to 20 lbs of wheat. In future players will receive movement and exhaustion penalties based on what they are carrying in their hands etc, and there will be a hygeine and filth consideration there, but its early days atm.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/40695630/4a547235dec3fdeb16f1b431742b10b841134f71.png[/img]
That's the roughly farming as it currently stands.
[/olist]

Crops only gain growth progress provided they are watered. They cannot die to not being watered yet. Something that I will be experimenting with later is the progression of blight and disease, and how it can propagate through crop fields.

Handling anything that needs to propagate at scale will need a lot of investigation into on the CPU, GPU, and networking sides because its very prone to rapidly scaling out of control performance wise. The same goes for fire, and disease spread between animals.

[h2] Labor and time [/h2]
The goal with this farming method is for it to actually be quite laborious. That way, each "break point" will feel fulfilling. The idea is that the player will progress like so:

1. Hand farming
2. Better tools
3. NPC assistance
4. Animal / beast of burden assistance (ploughs etc)
5. Full farming automation.

And hopefully at each break through the player will feel as if they have really taken a load off their back.

[h2] Future optimizations[/h2]
I also haven't performed any major optimizations on these yet, and the systems are very heavy in performance. I have several ideas for major optimizations, both in the GPU, CPU, and network side.

Something I want to experiment with is streaming "big data" down Unreals networking stack in a way that doesn't choke out the connections, and allows for late joiners. It's a tall order - but Unreal can do it.

[h2] Community! [/h2]
Thank you for reading. 
[url=https://discord.gg/BpatzE5PnD]Join the Discord![/url].

Going forward I want to include the change list with each dev update post. These changes are old, but I'm including them here for the especially curious.

notes.title: DevUpdate: Biomes
notes.content:
[b]Howdy everyone![/b]

For the last few days I've been working on setting up our games biomes and some basic biome interaction, check out the following WIP images of our biomes so far!

[h2]Biome spawning and layout[/h2]
To spawn the biomes into the game world, I've taken a "temperature" + "wetness" approach so far, and its giving quite decent results. Basically, the further from the equator of the map you are, the colder the temperature  gets, and the further inland you are, the dryer the map gets - multiplying these two together allows us to determine which biome you're in.

The biome layout, their flora, and fauna all spawn procedurally, and so will be totally different based on your map seed. Right now this map seed isn't exposed to the player - but we see no reason why not to expose that in the future :)

My goal is to hopefully ensure that pretty much every map seed has a good variation and scattering of biomes, as well as their sizes. Right now the generator needs a little more work - because a lot of seeds end up simply generating heaps of open and empty ocean :(.

[h2]Macro level world[/h2]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/oioqryc.png[/img]
[i]A continental shelf, approx 4+km wide ingame.[/i]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/Cb58ac4.png[/img]
[i]You can clearly see the biome separations here, between the central hot climates, and then the more temperate climates as you head north or south - ending with boreal and tundra biomes at the edges of the map.[/i]

[img]https://i.imgur.com/hWxnO0w.png[/img]
[i]World overview.[/i]

[h2]Temperate Forest[/h2]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/dEzVYmK.png[/img]

[h3]Forest flora[/h3]
Grass is incredibly thick and tall in the forest biome. The sun is blocked by the above tree canopy, and the density of lumber and smaller forgeable bushes is crazy high.

The forest is a bountiful place - plenty of forgeable food can be found there in the form of berries, mushrooms etc - but it is also the home to most of the games animals, so by virtue will be quite dangerous.

[h3]Forest fauna[/h3]
Wolves, bears, boar, and deer, can all be found in the forest biome. Every so often, the game world checks to see if the player is in a particular biome, and attempts to spawn an animal around them.

The animal needs enough free space from other animals and humans in order to succeed in spawning - and different animals have different chances to spawn. For example, chickens are far more common then wolves are, and bears are exceptionally rare.

[h2]Grasslands[/h2]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/U2OoDek.png[/img]

[h3]Grasslands flora[/h3]
The grasslands are a deceptively simple biome. It doesn't really provide many naturally found resources in the way of forgeable or harvestable plants, there are however some flowers that can be plucked for use in late game dyes.

However, it makes up for that in its geography - providing excellent places to build, and fertile lands to farm. It mostly shines as a fauna based biome.

[h3]Grasslands fauna[/h3]
The grasslands are home to the grazing animals. Bison, horses, rabbits, chickens, etc. I've set up the grass biomes to be not particularly rewarding, but not particularly threatening either. 

In fair weather, you should be able to survive in a grass biome just fine, but without lumber to build a shelter, and without a long term food option, its going to be hard to survive without leaving the grasslands biome. 

Eventually, you will be able to return to the grasslands in order to tame a worthwhile horse, or to domesticate sheep, goats, and other grazers.

--- 
Currently, the below biomes haven't much/any content developed for them, but I'll follow this dev blog up in the near future with what content we're going to be putting into these other biomes - and what makes them unique from the other more temperate biomes:

[h2]Plains[/h2]
[img]https://i.imgur.com/cvC0FHK.png[/img]
Currently, the plains only spawn the odd tree, as well as some grass for animals to graze. So I'm going to be updating this biome pretty substantially in the near future as I figure out exactly what belongs to this biome in terms of gameplay.

[h2]Desert[/h2]
Our initial thoughts for the desert were to make it an abundant source of natural minerals, like iron, and copper - etc, along with salt, and potentially some other naturally occurring spices used in late game recipes and foods. 

[h2]Boreal forest[/h2]

[img] https://i.imgur.com/x6nEE2Q.png [/img]
[i]A southern ice shelf continent. White = Tundra, Dark green = Boreal forest[/i]

Probably the most 'extreme' environment that a player will actually manage to survive in long term. Exactly what the boreal forests offer players when compared to more temperate areas is yet to be determined.

[h2]Tundra[/h2]
The goal with tundra is mainly to ensure players aren't able to venture outside of the world. The idea being that "survival" in the tundra is basically impossible. 

We haven't thought too much about the tundra biome, but as we work on it, we will update you all in a future post.

[h2]Wetlands[/h2]
Lastly, the map doesn't spawn proper "rivers" or "lakes" yet - but that's something I'm going to be exploring in the near future. I want to create a specific biome that exists around bodies of water, flowing rivers, etc, that provides an abundance of fishing opportunities as well as some bears opportunistically hunting in the rivers.

Hopefully, if we do our job right, our players will find ample areas that provide either strong tactical position, challenging gameplay, or fun roleplay opportunities throughout our biomes for founding towns and cities.

---

Alright well that's everything for the biome update so far! We still have lots of other extra content to show off, but we're going to detail that in dedicated posts rather then lumping them all in together. Also - I'll make sure to follow up with a biomes pt2 post when the other areas are more fleshed out, so stay tuned!

[h1]Follow along the development![/h1]
Remember as always, if you want to influence the direction of the game, then please either jump in the discord and come say hi, or feel free to post in the steam community!

Discord: [url=https://discord.gg/JcfBtQn]Join Discord![/url]
